metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.5 or lower) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak values.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >80), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5–10% below peak or adjust downward by 2–3 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop — increase forecast downward bias by 1–2% per day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to overfit recent volatility — smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum after a dip, model often lags — add 1–2 days of upward momentum to forecast, especially if sentiment is positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates late-period spikes (last 5–7 days) — increase forecast by 2–5% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often misreads sentiment — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days to avoid overconfidence.
